items.note: Krishna III's expedition into Mālwā against the Paramāra Siyaka, possibly prompted by Siyaka's title Maharājādhirājapati proclaiming his independence.
Metrical portion introduces three kings, Bappaiparāja, Vairisinha and Siyaka, each son and successor of the former.
Siyaka, father of Vākpati-Muñja, held the throne at least from 949 to 969 A.C., from grants of V. 1005, 1026 and Muñja's grants of 1031-1043.
Footnote: the royal genealogy in the Udaipur praśasti (No. 24) has two more members, Vairisinha (I) and Siyaka (I), before Vakpati (I), for whom no historical fact is given.

claim.value: genealogy in Udaipur prasasti (No. 24) lists two extra predecessors, Vairisinha (I) and Siyaka (I)

items.note: Editor's reconstruction: Bappaiparāja began c. 900 A.C.; Vairisiṃha entered Mālava; Sīyaka established himself there, capturing Ujjain probably from a Pratīhāra governor.
The Chandēlla territory is said to have then extended up to Vidishā in the south-west.

items.note: Vākpatirāja's Dharampurī grant dated 14th of bright Bhādrapada, year 1031, equated with 3 September 974 A.C. or 23 August 975 A.C.
Genealogy Vākpatirāja alias Amōghavarsha, Siyaka, Vairisiṃha, Kṛishṇarāja; house identified as Paramāras of Mālwā from the Garuḍa symbol.
Dharampurī grant is the first issued by Vākpatirāja alias Muñja, V.S. 1031 = 975 A.C., and the first royal charter issued from Mālwā, earlier ones being from Gujarāt.
